hyps.why: With edge 5 absent, removing the direct 0->3 path leaves only edge 4 feeding the output, risking disconnection or a severe capacity collapse.
Without the direct input-output edge, removing edge 5 eliminates one of very few remaining paths into node 3.
When edge 3 is absent, edge 4 is a key route to the output, so deleting it hurts much more.
Edge 0 feeds both 1->3 and 1->2->3 paths, so zeroing node 1 is catastrophic when the direct 0->3 path is missing.
Replacing none adds a whole new learned path to the output, a larger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Avg pooling on the direct path is among the weakest choices, so upgrading it to a 3x3 conv yields the biggest improvement.
If edge 5 is none, node 2 never reaches the output, so changing edge 1 has almost no effect.
With edge 0 none, node 1 is zero, so a conv on 1->2 contributes nothing.
With edge 0 none, node 1 carries no signal, so a conv on 1->3 cannot help.
If edge 5 is none, node 2 is a dead end, so improving edge 2 has negligible effect on accuracy.
